title: Evaluating supply chain resilience during pandemic using agent-based simulation
short_title: Supply chain resilience during pandemics via agent-based simulation
journal: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
abstract: Recent pandemics have highlighted vulnerabilities in our global economic systems, especially supply chains. A possible future pandemic raises a dilemma for business owners between short-term profitability and long-term supply chain resilience preparedness. In this study, we propose a novel agent-based simulation model that integrates epidemiological dynamics using a Susceptible–Exposed–Infected–Recovered–Dead (SEIRD) model, a supply and demand economic model, and a spatial representation of supply chain networks to evaluate supply chain resilience preparedness strategies during pandemics. Using this model, we explore a range of supply chain resilience preparedness strategies under pandemic scenarios using in silico experiments. Our analysis shows that the exact supply chain resilience preparedness strategy is hard to obtain for each firm and is relatively sensitive to the exact profile of the pandemic and economic state at the beginning of the pandemic. As such, we used a machine learning model that uses agent-based simulation to estimate a near-optimal supply chain resilience preparedness strategy for a firm.
summary: Pandemics expose weaknesses in supply chains and leave business owners torn between short-term profit and long-term resilience. We built an agent-based simulation combining an epidemic model, a supply and demand economic model and a spatial supply chain network to test preparedness strategies. The best strategy proved hard to pin down and sensitive to the pandemic's profile and the starting economic state, so we used machine learning with the simulation to estimate a near-optimal strategy for a firm.
key_findings: The model integrates a SEIRD epidemic model (susceptible, exposed, infected, recovered, dead), a supply and demand model, and spatial supply chain networks.
The exact best preparedness strategy is hard to obtain for each firm and is sensitive to the pandemic profile and initial economic state.
A machine learning model using the agent-based simulation estimates a near-optimal supply chain resilience preparedness strategy for a firm.
